primary_diagnosis_treated: Cardiorenal syndrome (type 2 myocardial injury secondary to CKD‑5, anemia, possible heart failure)
nice_guideline_used: NG106 (Chronic heart failure), NG203 (Chronic kidney disease)

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after liver function reassessment
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD stage 5 (CV‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends a statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.duration: Lifelong — titrate to target HR <70 bpm, review annually
medications.purpose: Improves survival and reduces hospitalisation in HFrEF
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 lists beta‑blockers as first‑line disease‑modifying therapy for HFrEF

medications.medication: Valsartan 320 mg / Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg oral tablet
medications.duration: Lifelong — monitor renal function and potassium 1‑2 weeks after any change, then 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin system blockade for HF and CKD; thiazide adds modest BP control
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 (ARB as first‑line when ACE‑I intolerant) and NG203 (ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with hypertension)

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily (titrate up to 80 mg twice daily based on congestion)
medications.duration: Lifelong — review 1‑2 weeks after initiation and after each titration, then 3‑monthly
medications.purpose: Relieve fluid overload (edema, dyspnoea) in heart failure; safe at eGFR 7 mL/min
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 recommends loop diuretics for symptomatic fluid overload in HF

medications.dose: 1 g every 6 hours as needed, maximum 3 g per day
medications.purpose: Pain control for osteoarthritis; safe alternative to NSAIDs in CKD and HF
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 advises avoidance of chronic NSAIDs in CKD; paracetamol is recommended instead

medications.dose: 0.4 mg spray as needed for angina
medications.purpose: Relief of acute chest pain (ischemic heart disease)
medications.nice_justification: Guideline‑based symptomatic therapy for angina (standard of care)
NICE recommends low‑dose aspirin for secondary CV prevention in IHD
Standard therapy for Alzheimer’s; not covered by HF/CKD guidelines but required for comorbidity

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined loop and thiazide diuretics increase risk of hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia and volume depletion
interactions_checked.action: Monitor serum electrolytes and renal function 1‑2 weeks after start; reduce thiazide dose if hypokalaemia develops

interactions_checked.interaction: Concurrent diuretic and ARB can precipitate acute kidney injury if volume depleted
interactions_checked.action: Ensure euvolemia before initiating; check creatinine and potassium 1‑2 weeks after start

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive negative inotropic effect may worsen bradycardia or hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure after titration; adjust doses if symptomatic

interactions_checked.interaction: NSAIDs may increase statin‑related myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue naproxen (see contraindications) and use paracetamol instead

contraindications.reason: Chronic NSAID use is contraindicated in CKD stage 5 and heart failure (NICE NG106, NG203)
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol up to 3 g/day for osteoarthritis pain

contraindications.reason: Duplicate statin therapy increases risk of myopathy and liver injury; only one high‑intensity statin should be used

assumptions_warnings: Left‑ventricular ejection fraction not provided – assumed HFrEF based on history of MI and elevated troponin; echocardiogram required.
Serum potassium level not available – baseline potassium needed before any dose change of ARB/diuretic and before considering MRA.
Full liver function tests (ALT, AST, ALP, GGT) not available – elevated bilirubin noted; statin therapy should be held until LFTs are reviewed.
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) not available – required before initiating IV iron or ESA for anaemia.
Allergy status not documented – verify no allergy to statins, sulfonamides (IV iron), or paracetamol before prescribing.
Blood pressure is low‑normal (104/66 mmHg); careful titration of diuretics required to avoid symptomatic hypotension.
treatment_summary: The plan addresses cardiorenal syndrome by continuing guideline‑recommended ARB, beta‑blocker, and high‑intensity statin (after liver review), adding a low‑dose loop diuretic for congestion, and replacing the contraindicated naproxen with paracetamol. Duplicate simvastatin is stopped. Monitoring includes renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, and heart rate after each change, with regular follow‑up and urgent referral for echocardiography and nephrology input.
